qs.q: Which of the following virological characteristics is shared by all viral haemorrhagic fever viruses?
o: They are single-stranded RNA, enveloped viruses
They have a high infectivity dose requiring many particles
They are easily transmitted through aerosols except for Dengue
Humans serve as their primary natural reservoirs in nature
qs.e: Viral haemorrhagic fever viruses are single stranded RNA and enveloped. They have a low infectivity dose of 1-10 viruses and humans are only accidentally infected rather than being natural reservoirs.

qs.q: A nurse sustains a needle-stick injury while caring for a patient with suspected viral haemorrhagic fever. What is the immediate first step for management of this mucocutaneous exposure?
o: Immediately wash skin with soap and water and flush eyes
Administer a prophylactic dose of intravenous antibiotics
Place the healthcare worker in a negative pressure room
Draw baseline viral serology before any local wound care
qs.e: For percutaneous or mucocutaneous exposures, the immediate step is to wash the affected skin with soap and water and flush the eyes. High-risk exposures are then placed under medical surveillance.

qs.q: In the event of suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, how should laboratory specimens be handled and transported?
o: Clearly identified, double bagged, and hand carried
Sent via the standard pneumatic tube delivery system
Placed in a single plastic container with stickers
Stored in a standard refrigerator on the ward unit
qs.e: All specimens for suspected viral haemorrhagic fevers should be clearly identified, double bagged, and hand carried to the lab because they are highly infectious in the lab setting.

qs.q: Which of the following viral haemorrhagic fevers has a widely available live attenuated vaccine providing protection for up to 30-35 years?
qs.e: Yellow fever has a live attenuated single-dose vaccine that confers immunity in 1 week in 95% of people and protects for 30-35 years. Vaccines for Dengue and Rift Valley fever are still under trial or unavailable.
